brief: CRITIC round 1 over W1-17 — dialogue (topic graph, rumours, voice, CONSUMPTION)
measured_at_commit: 6c979e3 (working tree — W1-17 is uncommitted, so every number is a claim about the tree, not a commit; RULES 12)
contention: node tools/contention.mjs --gate returned exit 3 (5 browser instances, load 4.80/core). This was a text-only audit and I ran NO browser. I changed no engine file so no boot-check was owed. RI-DLG01 step 5b/5c (runtime combat lockout) and step 6 (blind topology pairing) are recorded as NOT RUN, not as passes.
findings: CONFIRMED, the round's most consequential claim: `r` (Morrowind CS filter field 2, Race) is authored on 0 of 1,280 infos; every race gate is spelt requires.race (138) / forbids.race (40), which is what infoAllowed() reads. The pre-fix lint was blind to all 178 and its 105 findings were false. Independent instrument: tools/dialogue/critic-field-census.mjs, break arm re-spells requires.race as `r` and the census sees it.

HEADLINE FINDING: 133 of 1,280 infos (10.4%) can be heard by NO player from ANY speaker, against a reported 3. Measured by tools/dialogue/critic-reach.mjs over 347 real speakers x a 5,400-player space (10 races x 4 upbringings x 15 dispositions x 9 knowledge sets, domains read out of the corpus). Causes: 40 written for actors no NPC is, 90 gated to an (actor, town) pair no such actor stands in, 3 always outscored. Break arm: forcing player gates true moves it to 226 and the 'always outscored' bucket 3 -> 96.

BIGGEST GAP: `magister` — RI-DLG06 §B row 2, the Telvanni-analogue, one of the six required archetypes — is authored on 23 infos and NO NPC in the 347-person roster carries that actor. voice-metrics.mjs measures its register and speakers.json sets its bands and not a line can reach a player. A topic `magister-varo-dren` answers 'I am he' and Varo Dren is not in the roster. Nine of the forty are near-misses: notary-sedda-vell exists tagged `archivist`, harbourmistress-tesh exists tagged `clerk`, eleven scribes exist tagged `clerk`.

ROOT CAUSE: RI-DLG01 §A mandates first-match-wins and converse.js:284 scores specificity instead. Measured over 75,948 resolutions: 0 decided by a tie, and the two rules disagree on 52 answers. So (a) the unreachable-INFO lint tests a rule the engine does not implement; (b) order-infos.mjs --write was ARITHMETICALLY INCAPABLE of changing an answer, so answer-census.mjs --diff's '0 of 75,151 changed' was forced before it ran and is not evidence of care; (c) shadow-audit.mjs audits only the 3 records the lint nominated and can never find what the lint missed. Instrument: tools/dialogue/critic-semantics.mjs, break arm compares the shipped rule to itself and gets 0 divergence.

orphans_npc_advertised: 23 — honest disclosure, wrong bucket. RI-DLG01 §D excludes only roots and journal-added from the orphan definition; npc.topics is neither, so on the item's plain words these are orphans and the zero-tolerance row fails. Verdict records orphans: 23. The builder found the fourth door, built the detector and headlined the count, which is the opposite of hiding.

Behind it: topicsFor() offers npc.topics WITHOUT intersecting against player.topics_known (only the nine roots are gated). A cold player is offered a mean of 1.66 topics per person and 126 of 468 topics (26.9%) are obtainable without ever learning the word. build-graph's reachable_only_via_another_topic 0.9808 is a property of the diagram; through the reader that runs it is 0.731.

TWO CONSUMPTION HOLES, proven by paired control (positive controls move 75,948 and 47,273 answers): `res` — Morrowind's RESULT SCRIPT, on 13 infos, which RI-DLG01 §A pairs with AddTopic as the item's most important structural fact — moves 0 answers. infoFor() does not carry it out of the reader at all, so 13 topics authored to open a journal entry when asked about cannot. `f` (filter field 4, Faction, 4 infos) likewise. consume.mjs has an arm for neither, no arm for rumours.json at all, and no --break flag. This is the twentieth authored-model-with-no-reader and it is in W1-17's own data.

answer-census.mjs PLAYERS (imported by shadow-audit.mjs and copied by consume.mjs) uses upbringings marsh/town/legion/coast. The canonical roster is interior/lukiul/foreign-born/blackrose and character/reaction.js raceTerm() THROWS on all four. The project's census, its shadow audit and its CONSUMPTION tool all run characters the game cannot construct; the 3 requires.upbringing infos can never fire in any of them and no census player exceeds disposition 70, so the seven d:80 infos are invisible.

VOICE INSTRUMENT: `second_regex` appears 0 times in voice-metrics.mjs, and so do lexicon, lexicon_min_markers, lexicon_min_lift, friend_per_1k_max and centroid/variance. Five fields speakers.json declares for its own named checker are unread, and 2 of RI-DLG06 §B's 6 binding separation requirements are unimplemented. CONSEQUENCE: one of the builder's two headline self-reported failures is FALSE — the legionary grammar tic is reported at 0.00/1k and measures 5.12/1k against a 1.0 minimum once second_regex is evaluated and the anchored regex is applied per sentence rather than per entry. Same cause understates magister (1.48 vs 16.30) and archivist (3.32 vs 26.17). Only mudborn's tic (0.24/1k) genuinely fails.

CALIBRATION ACCEPTED, NOT FITTED: 3 of 5 §A reference speakers reproduce within 0.15 w/sent; Ajira misses by 0.78 and Nileno by 0.63, the tool prints '<-- disagrees' next to both and passes anyway. A tool tuned to its reference points would hit all five. 'Aryon 10.40 vs 10.40' is an artifact of the item quoting one decimal. STTR is correctly standardised over 500-token windows, which kills the obvious alternative explanation for the five STTR misses — those are real.

METRIC vs EAR on the three indistinguishable pairs: sapcutter/legionary is a METRIC DEFECT — statistically identical on all three axes and nothing alike to the ear (servile third-person self-reference at 24.05/1k against imperative-plus-'citizen'), because §B's separation rule offers two length measures and one diversity measure and NO measure of mood, while the corpus already holds the discriminating evidence in its own address and grammar_tic blocks. mudborn/archivist and rootkeeper/mudborn are GENUINE misses — the rhythm really is shared. So two pairs need a rewrite, not three, and the reference item needs a fourth axis.

AXIS I COULD NOT BREAK, reported as such: signposting. Tree-wide echo_direction is 1.23 per 10k words against check-prose.mjs's own Morrowind reference of 1.08 — SIX lines in 48,954 words. The brief's expected 'tree-wide 2.7' does not reproduce at this commit. Worst file is 07-root-coverage.json at 12.55/10k, which is two lines of 86 and one of them is safety advice. The signposting axis is a pass.

SECOND AXIS I COULD NOT BREAK: I hypothesised the author's hand showing through six mouths and built tools/dialogue/critic-figures.mjs to catch it. 05-asking-around.json has the highest terminal-question rate of any file (20.6%) — but split per actor, in-file against out-of-file, rootkeeper is 0/10 vs 1%, mudborn 0/3 vs 3%, archivist 0/1 vs 1%. The file's rate is its ACTOR MIX, not a figure pushed into quiet mouths. REFUTED, and it is a credit to the round. The antithesis figure likewise varies by archetype, not by file.

PROSE: genuinely excellent and the strongest axis in the project. Read all 63 infos of 05-asking-around.json, all 23 magister lines, five full root-topic info stacks and ~60 rumours. No signposting, no helpfulness, speaker-owned sentences, a world that contradicts itself on the record. Only charge: sapcutter ends 43.1% of its 116 lines by asking the player a direct question — characterisation that has become a sentence template. Not this round's authoring.

topics/thorn.json: four rows on a topic/text/links schema that no loader reads ('Walk the boards, not the ground. The ground here has opinions.'). The round filed this as its 'second tool defect' and fixed it by making build-graph.mjs skip them too, so 'the two loaders now agree' — they agree to ignore live prose. Its links point at my-kingdom and the-marsh, BOTH of which are on the orphans_npc_advertised list.

NUMBERS THAT DO NOT REPRODUCE AS PUBLISHED, all minor against a very honest baseline: (1) Lilmoth's rumour pool is 24 -> 26 -> 28 -> 28 -> 30 with exactly the four flags named, not 24 -> 26 -> 28 -> 29 -> 32; folding in act_two_closed and act_three_closed gives 24 -> 26 -> 29 -> 30 -> 32, so the measurement omits two flags it depended on (RULES 12). (2) check-dialogue-topics warnings are 30, not 32 — the status file says both. (3) 'All 17 new warnings are the cell ladder' is 18 of 19; the exception is soulrest/rootkeeper, a disposition ladder (d:30 vs d:20) rather than a cell one. No shared gate was weakened; I checked.

RumourBook.for() CONSUMPTION independently reproduced by perturbation rather than by reading the diff: stripping every knows gate flattens Lilmoth to 36 across all five act states while the shipped file moves 24 -> 30, and every one of the nine settlements moves. This was a real nineteenth dead model caught before it shipped and is the strongest single thing in the round.

W1-09 CONFLICT CONFIRMED UNCHANGED: game/data/combat/parley.json is total_f 78 / stamina 0 against RI-DLG09's 102 f@60 / stamina 20 on f13 / arm 1-12 free-cancel / 5 routes. Scored 0 in its own reference-item row and DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the min-over-axes: W1-09 owns the file and the builder declared the conflict rather than editing a neighbour's file. Filed as a cross-piece debt for an arbiter.

RULE 4 COMPLIANCE: all four critic instruments have --break arms and all four were run. critic-field-census --break re-spells requires.race as `r` and exits 1. critic-semantics --break compares the shipped rule to itself and gets 0 divergence. critic-reach --break forces every player gate true and the 'always outscored' bucket goes 3 -> 96 (the count goes UP, not down, and the tool's own header explains why). critic-figures --break separates a 100%-figure corpus from a 0%-figure one.

RULES 17, OBSERVED IN THE WILD DURING THIS RUN: `node tools/ownership.mjs --staged critic-w1-17` reported 21 staged paths declared by twelve other live pieces, so I committed by explicit pathspec rather than committing the index. Before that commit landed, a neighbour’s own `git add -A` had already swept my verdict, my nine artifacts and this status file into 24a82aa. Both halves of rule 17 fired in one run: the check saved twelve neighbours from me, and nothing saved me from the thirteenth. The content is intact and verified byte-identical; only the attribution is wrong.
next_step: Round 2 builder: (1) decide first whether infoFor() implements RI-DLG01 §A's first-match-wins or the item is amended to the scoring rule — every instrument in round 1 was built on the losing side of that disagreement; (2) close the actor roster so critic-reach's 'no such actor' bucket is 0; (3) give `res` a reader; (4) make voice-metrics read second_regex and the lexicon rules and re-report the miss list. An arbiter owes a ruling on RI-DLG09 vs W1-09.
note_on_shared_files: reports/blog-feed.jsonl is append-only and is shared by every piece; one line appended, nothing rewritten. corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-17-r1/ and reports/critic-w1-17/ are new directories created by this critic. I edited NO file under game/ and no authored dialogue — the four instruments are read-only over the shipped data and import the shipped readers rather than re-implementing them (RULES 10). tools/dialogue/critic-*.mjs are new files in a directory W1-17 also writes to; the names are prefixed `critic-` precisely so the two sets never collide.
shot: None. This is a text audit, contention was at ceiling and I launched no browser; the round's illustrative image is the builder's own docs/shots/2026-08-08-w1-17-topic-graph-and-the-acts.png. Reported rather than faked (RULES 26).

commits.verdict_md_json_status_artifacts: 24a82aa — NOT MINE. A neighbouring agent ran `git add -A` while I was writing my commit message and swept corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-17-r1.{md,json}, all nine files under artifacts/W1-17-r1/ and this status file into its own commit, under the message “Two ledgers disagreed by 53% and nothing in the tree read both”. Content verified byte-identical to my final versions and the verdict still validates from HEAD; nothing was lost, only attribution. This is the exact failure RULES 17 was rewritten for, recorded here rather than silently, as 6c979e3 did for an earlier instance.
commits.instruments: c36653e / 173ee86 — the orchestrator’s own bank commits, which took tools/dialogue/critic-{field-census,semantics,reach,figures}.mjs mid-run. Legitimate banking, named as such.
